- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing sharp drops.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peaks at 1.2x recent high if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.67 to -0.33 within 3 days), model often fails to revert; apply mean reversion correction to 3–5 day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); reduce by 2–5% if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate; add 3–6% to forecast to account for suppressed volatility.
